scenes.narration: Go to bed and wake up at the same time, every day. Weekends too.
Matthew Walker's most repeated advice is consistency. Your body runs on an internal daily clock.

lines: and when to wake you up

scenes.narration: A regular bedtime and wake time help that clock know when to make you sleepy, and when to make you alert.
Sleep in late at the weekend, then get up early on Monday, and you shift that clock back and forth. It's a bit like mild jet lag.
A steady schedule is one of the simplest habits for better sleep. If sleep problems carry on despite good habits, see a doctor.
Set a fixed wake up time for the next seven days, weekend included, and keep it even after a poor night.
This is general information, not medical advice.
